chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Mārid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about the ʿaqīqah.

He said: “A sheep, or a cow, or a camel. Then he names the child, shaves the head of the newborn on the seventh day, and gives charity in gold or silver equal to the weight of its hair. If the child is male, a male animal is sacrificed on his behalf, and if female, a female animal is sacrificed on her behalf.”

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: a camel offered as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.ذَهَبًا: gold given as charity according to the weight of the hair
key_terms.شَاةٌ: a sheep suitable for the ʿaqīqah offering
key_terms.فِضَّةً: silver given as charity according to the weight of the hair
key_terms.يَوْمَ ٱلسَّابِعِ: the seventh day after birth, the prescribed time mentioned here
key_terms.ٱلْعَقِيقَةِ: the sacrificial offering made for a newborn child
key_terms.ٱلْمَوْلُودِ: the newborn child for whom the rite is performed

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings of ʿaqīqah for a newborn in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the rulings of ʿaqīqah for a newborn, including the types of animals that may be offered, naming the child, shaving the head on the seventh day, and giving charity equal to the weight of the hair. It also specifies matching the sex of the sacrificial animal to that of the child.
